summary.text: Susan Collins is the Republican U.S. Senator from Maine, first elected in 1996 and now in her fifth term. A native of Caribou, she worked for Sen. William Cohen, held Maine and federal appointive posts and ran unsuccessfully for governor in 1994 before entering the Senate. She chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee and is seeking a sixth term.

paragraphs.text: Born December 7, 1952, in Caribou, Maine, one of six children; her family runs a lumber business founded in 1844, and both parents served as mayor of Caribou. She graduated from Caribou High School in 1971.
Graduated Phi Beta Kappa from St. Lawrence University in 1975.

Began working for Maine Rep. William Cohen in 1975 and stayed on his staff when he was elected to the Senate, becoming staff director of the Oversight of Government Management Subcommittee of the Committee on Governmental Affairs.

Appointed Commissioner of the Maine Department of Professional and Financial Regulation by Gov. John McKernan in 1987, and director of the Small Business Administration's New England regional office by President George H.W. Bush in 1992.

Served as a deputy state treasurer of Massachusetts in 1993 (Wikipedia). She was the Republican nominee for governor of Maine in 1994, the first woman nominated by a major party for the post, finishing third with 23% of the vote.
Became founding executive director of the Center for Family Business at Husson College (now Husson University) in 1994.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 1996, succeeding Cohen, and re-elected in 2002, 2008, 2014 and 2020; her Senate biography says she was the first Republican woman to win a fifth term.

Chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee (since January 2025) and also serves on the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions and Intelligence committees. Her Senate biography says she has cast more than 10,000 consecutive votes.
According to her Senate biography, she is married to Thomas A. Daffron and lives in Bangor, Maine.
